note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

chapters.title: Part 1: Life is long if you know how to use it

episodes.title: Life isn't short
episodes.hook: Life isn't short. You're just spending it badly.
episodes.angle: We are given enough time; we waste a lot of it. Example: someone who 'has no time' but has 6 hours of screen time.

episodes.title: The time thief
episodes.hook: You'd never let a stranger take your money. You let them take your time.
episodes.angle: People guard their wallets but give away hours without thinking. Example: saying yes to a pointless meeting you'd never pay to attend.

episodes.title: Count your real years
episodes.hook: You might be forty, but how many years did you actually live?
episodes.angle: Subtract the hours lost to other people's demands, worry and distraction. Example: a quick count of a typical week's lost hours.

episodes.title: The busy trap
episodes.hook: Being busy is the laziest way to waste your life.
episodes.angle: Busyness feels important but leaves no room to live. Example: a manager who answers emails at his daughter's recital.

episodes.title: 'When I retire'
episodes.hook: 'I'll live when I retire' is the most dangerous plan you have.
episodes.angle: Postponing life assumes a future nobody promised you. Example: the person saving the trip to Japan for 'later', every year.

episodes.title: Tomorrow steals today
episodes.hook: The biggest waste of time is waiting for tomorrow.
episodes.angle: Expectation of the future makes us lose the present. Example: scrolling while 'waiting for motivation' to start the project.

episodes.title: Live like it's borrowed
episodes.hook: Your time isn't yours. It's on loan, and nobody told you the due date.
episodes.angle: Treat each day as limited and it gets valuable. Example: how differently you spend your last day before moving abroad.

episodes.title: Start one thing today
episodes.hook: Pick the thing you've been 'about to start' for a year. Start it tonight.
episodes.angle: Living begins the moment you stop rehearsing. Example: writing one ugly page of the novel instead of planning it.

chapters.title: Part 3: Who you give your days to

episodes.title: Everybody wants a piece of you
episodes.hook: Look at your calendar. Whose life is it?
episodes.angle: Many people spend their days serving others' ambitions and their own vanity. Example: a calendar full of things done to impress people you don't like.

episodes.title: Saying no is a skill
episodes.hook: Every yes to them is a no to yourself.
episodes.angle: Protecting your time is not selfish, it's the only way to have a life. Example: declining a favour politely and using the hour to call your grandma.

episodes.title: Fake leisure
episodes.hook: Your hobby might just be another job.
episodes.angle: Even 'free time' can be anxious and busy, collecting things or chasing status. Example: a gym session spent filming yourself for likes.

episodes.title: The rich who are poor
episodes.hook: Some of the richest people you know have no time at all.
episodes.angle: Money bought with all your time is a bad trade. Example: the founder who can afford a beach house he never visits.

chapters.title: Part 4: The part of life nobody can take

episodes.title: The past is safe
episodes.hook: Your past is the only thing nobody can take from you.
episodes.angle: Reflecting on lived time turns it into a possession; busy people never look back. Example: an old man flipping through a photo album versus one who can't remember last year.

episodes.title: Read the dead
episodes.hook: You can have a conversation with the smartest people who ever lived. Tonight.
episodes.angle: Reading great minds adds their years to yours. Example: ten minutes with an old book instead of a feed.

episodes.title: Old age is not proof
episodes.hook: Grey hair doesn't mean someone lived long. Just that they existed long.
episodes.angle: Length of life is not the same as amount of life. Example: two ninety-year-olds, one full, one empty.

episodes.title: The question at the end
episodes.hook: On your last day, what will you wish you had done with today?
episodes.angle: Judge today by how it looks from the end. Example: imagining your 80-year-old self watching you today.
